newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-AUSTRALIA IN DAVIS CUP QUARTER FINAL WIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AUSTRALIA IN DAVIS CUP QUARTER FINAL WIN.

text.p: Todd Woodbridge and Mark Woodforde gave Australia a 3-0 quarter final Davis Cup win against the Czech Republic on Saturday but the world number one pair were pushed harder than expected in their doubles match.
Czech due Martin Damm and David Rikl surprised their hosts by taking the first set at Memorial Drive before capitulating 4-6 6-1 7-5 6-4 on the grass centre court.
Pat Rafter and Mark Philippoussis both won their singles rubbers on Friday to set Australia on the way to a semi-final meeting with either the United States or the Netherlands.
Woodbridge was Australia's weak link in the opening set, twice dropping his serve to allow the unfancied Czech pair an ideal start.
But the Australians gradually asserted their domination as Woodbridge found his timing and touch with both his serve and service returns.

The Czechs, already weakened by the decision of several top players including veteran Petr Korda to make themselves unavailable, suffered another setback on Friday when singles player Jiri Novak was forced to withdraw because of a virus.
The two sides will play two reverse dead singles rubbers on Sunday.
Australia upset Davis Cup holders France, also on grass, in the previous round two months ago in Sydney.
